name: Chainer
title: Master of Dementia
summary: A gifted summoner of nightmares whose friendship with Kamahl could not save him from the Mirari's influence.
biography: Chainer trained within the Cabal of Otaria, using dementia magic to summon nightmarish creatures from his mind.

Chainer discovered the Mirari in an abandoned mansion and presented it to the Cabal Patriarch. He and Kamahl formed an unexpected friendship in the pits, but his loyalty to the Cabal and growing distrust of its leadership eventually separated their paths.

Chainer used the Mirari to displace the Patriarch and overwhelm Cabal City with nightmares drawn through dementia magic. As his body was overtaken by the creatures he could no longer control, Kamahl killed him in an act of mercy. His downfall became one of the defining tragedies of the Odyssey block.

Skellum’s teaching introduced Chainer to a discipline that required carefully forming and controlling imagined horrors. Within the Cabal’s arena economy, success with that magic also made his talent more valuable to leaders who treated spectacular violence as a source of authority.

His friendship with Kamahl crossed institutional boundaries: a Pardic pit fighter and a Cabal summoner could care for one another without sharing the same understanding of where their loyalties belonged. That bond makes Chainer’s later attempt to master the Mirari a personal tragedy rather than a straightforward tale about a villain claiming an artifact.

The Torment card Chainer, Dementia Master translated his story into mechanics by creating a bond between Chainer and Nightmares that vanished with him. Wizards' design retrospective explains that the card was deliberately reserved for Torment because Chainer was the protagonist of Chainer's Torment. The card's rules communicate an idea about summoning, not the precise chronology of his death.

featuredCard.significance: Chainer's original Torment printing illustrates the Cabal summoner and his nightmarish magic.

source.title: Wizards of the Coast — Commander Masters Storyteller, Part 1
